title: Convex Optimization
relevance: Theorem 5.3, §5.2.3, printed pp. 226–227: for a convex problem Slater strict feasibility yields strong duality, and if the primal optimum is finite the dual optimum is attained. This applies to a finite SDP with affine equalities and a strictly feasible PSD-cone slack; it does not require the primal feasible set to be compact. It is the explicit one-sided attainment statement needed for the finite-SDP certificate argument, separate from strict positivity or Archimedean claims about a polynomial module.
lane: finite-SDP dual attainment under primal Slater

title: Semidefinite Programming
relevance: Theorem 3.1, printed pp. 64–65 (PDF pp. 16–17), states p*=d* if either the primal SDP is strictly feasible (F(x) ≻ 0) or the dual is strictly feasible; it states both optimal sets are nonempty when both sides are strictly feasible. This gives the finite-SDP cone interpretation and is not, by itself, the explicit one-sided dual-attainment statement supplied by Boyd–Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Theorem 5.3.
lane: finite-SDP dual attainment under primal Slater

title: Gradient of the Value Function in Parametric Convex Optimization Problems
relevance: Corollary 3, PDF p. 5, treats min_z 1/2 zᵀHz subject to Gz ≤ W+Sx, H ≻ 0, with a full-dimensional feasible parameter set X. Under LICQ at every feasible x, the value is C1 on int(X), with ∇V(x)=−Sᵀλ*(x); the proof uses continuous piecewise-affine primal and dual policies on critical regions. The gradient assertion excludes boundary points, so use on a closed master box needs an open feasible neighborhood or a separate boundary argument.
lane: parametric convex QP recourse and multiplier regularity

title: Lipschitz stability for a class of parametric optimization problems with polyhedral feasible set mapping
relevance: Corollary 3.1, article PDF p. 13, gives a polyhedral, upper-Lipschitz optimal-set mapping and Lipschitz value on bounded subsets for C ⪰ 0 and graph-convex polyhedral feasible maps. Remark 4.2(ii), PDF p. 19, adds that positive-definite QPs have a unique optimizer map that is Lipschitz on its domain, without LICQ. The result controls primal optimizer/value regularity, not multiplier continuity or differentiability of the value. Published online 25 Nov 2025, before the 2026-10-05 cutoff.
lane: parametric convex QP recourse and multiplier regularity

title: A ‘Joint+Marginal’ Approach to Parametric Polynomial Optimization
relevance: Theorem 3.5, arXiv PDF p. 11 (journal pp. 2005–2006), assumes the joint quadratic module is Archimedean and every parameter fiber is nonempty, with a known-moment absolutely continuous probability measure on the compact parameter set. Its total-degree SDP hierarchy gives polynomial lower approximants converging in integrated error and, after taking running maxima, almost uniformly to the recourse value. It gives no explicit order rate and does not hold private degree fixed.

title: Towards Global Solutions for Nonconvex Two-Stage Stochastic Programs: A Polynomial Lower Approximation Approach
authors: Zhong, Suhan and Cui, Ying and Nie, Jiawang
relevance: Theorem 4.1, journal p. 3490 (arXiv v3 PDF p. 14), assumes an Archimedean joint quadratic module and continuity of the recourse value on the feasible set; the polynomial lower approximations converge in L1 for a given probability measure as the total degree grows. Corollary 4.2, journal p. 3491, permits separate master/uncertainty degree schedules only while their minimum degree tends to infinity; the SOS certificate degree in private variables also grows. The theorem supplies no inverse-order rate, sparse gluing, or fixed-private-degree result.

title: Convergence rates for the moment-SoS hierarchy
authors: Schlosser, Corbinian and Tacchi-Bénard, Matteo and Lazarev, Alexey
relevance: Proposition 3.13, arXiv v3 p. 14, proves equivalence of an inward-pointing condition and Slater for the infinite-dimensional functional LP; their quantitative rate framework combines this with effective Putinar bounds and polynomial approximation. This Slater statement concerns the functional LP, not primal Slater for a finite moment SDP, and it is distinct from polynomial strict positivity or Archimedeanness of an SOS module. Theorem 3.8 is an approximation inequality, not the Slater result.
lane: Slater assumptions in moment-SOS rate theory

title: Convergence rate of the moment-SOS hierarchy for univariate polynomial optimization
authors: Henrion, Didier and Safey El Din, Mohab
relevance: Theorem 1, arXiv v1 p. 6, proves 0 ≤ e_r ≤ C/r² for every fixed univariate polynomial-optimization instance on a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of R described by arbitrary polynomial inequalities. C and the threshold r0 depend on the instance; this is not a uniform-in-data estimate. It is a direct stronger rate baseline for a one-variable ordinary quadratic module on a box, but gives no sparse-overlap, private-QP recourse, or multivariate result. The preprint was submitted 17 Sep 2026, before the cutoff.
lane: recent SOS rates and dimensional boundaries
